headline: South Korea's president said AI models are believed to have been used in some of the recent hacking attacks on the country's banks.
score_reason: Pool score kept: the president himself links AI to attacks on several banks; the AI link is still only 'believed' and no tools or breach size are given.
importance_line: The president now says AI is believed to have been used in attacks that exposed bank customers' personal data, which raises pressure on regulators and banks to strengthen their defences, but officials have not shown which AI tools were involved or how large the breaches are.
summary: Reuters reports, as carried by The Economic Times, that President Lee Jae Myung told a cabinet meeting on Tuesday 6 Oct 2026 that 'signs have emerged of AI being used' in some of the hacking incidents that exposed bank customers' personal information, and called for cybersecurity methods suited to the AI era. This continues the story we carried on 4 Oct 2026 about Lee ordering a full investigation into the data leaks; what is new is the president's own statement about AI, and Reuters notes that authorities have not yet disclosed which AI tools were used or how large the breaches are.
notes: Reuters page not openable (401); Reuters text read on The Economic Times copy; context from The Korea Times (Yonhap). Link kept at the Reuters original. Follow-up of the 4 Oct 2026 and 5 Oct 2026 Korean bank-hack items; same story line as C12-09 and C12-14.
